t1.text: 1 · Search tab: three plates above the native glass search field

s1a.text:
THE NATIVE SEARCH STAYS EXACTLY AS IT IS
RootView keeps .searchable on the TabView with .tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection). The field, its place at the bottom and the tab-bar morph are not touched. Only the idle content of SearchScreen changes: while the query is empty and the field is not focused, the same ScrollView that shows results today shows the three plates. Categories above, field below is the pattern the system search tab is built for, so the field does not need to move to the top.
STATES
• Idle: the plates.
• Field focused, nothing typed: today’s Recent list or hint. The plates cross-fade out (200 ms; Reduce Motion: no fade).
• Typing: today’s grouped results, unchanged.
• Clear or close: the plates return.
TO CHECK IN THE SIMULATOR
Reading focus inside SearchScreen: @Environment(\.isSearching) under a TabView-level searchable, or .searchFocused on RootView. If neither is reliable, fallback: the plates stay until the first character and Recent sits under them.

s1b.text:
LAYOUT A (RECOMMENDED) · METRICS
Title “Discover” / “Keşfet”: Literata 34/500, at the Library title position.
Plate: full width inside the 24 gutter, height 124, radius 16 continuous, 0.5 pt rule ring, 2 pt paper gap between strips. Short screens: height = min(124, 14 % of screen height), 95 on iPhone SE.
Label on paper, 10 under the plate: Literata 20/500 ink, then SF 13 ink2. Chevron 8 × 14 ink3. 22 between cards. No text on the images, no scrim, no glass on the cards.
The plate and its label are one button; pressed = opacity 0.85. VoiceOver: “Composers, 52 composers, button”; the images are decorative.
The scroll content ends above the field through the system safe area.
WHY A
Three equal items: no orphan cell (B) and no small images (C). Full-width strips let Eras read as a timeline and keep four faces legible. Everything fits without scrolling at 874 pt, and on SE with the shorter plate.
B keeps the two-column look of the reference but leaves Forms as the odd one. C keeps Recent visible but the collages become thumbnails.

s1c.text:
FREE USERS (PROPOSAL)
Today a free user who opens Search gets “Search is part of Premium” and the paywall opens by itself.
Proposed: browsing is open to everyone, like the Library and its filters. The plates, the lists and the era and form pages look the same for free and Premium; past pieces carry the Library lock and open the paywall, today’s piece opens.
Typing stays Premium: when a free user focuses the field, the screen shows today’s locked state (“Search is part of Premium”, See Premium) in place of Recent. The automatic paywall on opening the tab is removed.
NAVIGATION
The plates push inside the Search tab’s NavigationStack (a new router.searchPath). The bottom field stays on pushed pages, as the system does on a search tab (to verify); a non-empty query pops to the root and shows results. Pieces open through router.openPiece, as search results do today. Composer rows open the existing ComposerSheet.

s2a.text:
ERA COLLAGES: HOW THE PAINTINGS ARE PICKED
Picked by hand once and stored as piece ids (new content/eras.yaml, collage: four ids). The app uses those pieces’ existing thumbs, so no new image files.
1. The painting was made in the era itself. Many pairings are deliberately from another century; those are left out.
2. Four different painters, at least two composers.
3. One figure scene, one landscape, one interior where the era allows, so the strip is varied.
4. The subject must survive a narrow vertical crop: each pick gets a focal_x (new, 0–1), like focal_y on portraits.
5. No painting appears in two eras.
Renaissance has three pieces only; one of them is paired with Ingres (1814) because it shows the Sistine Chapel. It is used and flagged.
The picks come from the whole 200-piece catalogue, not only from published pieces, so the cards do not change every day.

s2b.text:
FORMS: THE THREE OPTIONS
1 · Music in paintings (recommended). The catalogue already holds paintings of people playing: Menzel’s flute concert, Danhauser’s Liszt at the piano, Mercier, Longhi, Zoffany, Lerolle. One per form, picked by hand (form_images in the same data file). All three cards then speak one visual language. Cost: symphony and orchestral works have no literal picture, so their picks are evocative, and eleven picks need Oytun’s eye.
2 · Stage plans. A small line drawing of who sits where: the orchestra’s arcs, four chairs for a quartet, a piano before the arcs. Drawn in ink on paper, in code (SwiftUI Canvas), no assets. It explains the form at a glance and is exact. Cost: a second visual language beside the paintings, and eleven drawings to design.
3 · Type only. The form name in large Literata with its count, no image. The quietest and cheapest. Cost: the Forms card looks empty beside two image cards.

s3a.text:
LISTS REUSE WHAT EXISTS
Composer row = LibraryRow geometry: 64 pt thumb (radius 8), SF 13 ink2 meta above, Literata 16/500 name, chevron. The thumb is the portrait, cover-cropped at focal_y. No portrait on file (Tallis, Pachelbel, Rodrigo, Barber): the stripe placeholder with the initial in Literata. A row opens the existing ComposerSheet.
Sort: the Library’s glass segmented control, A–Z | By era. By era groups chronologically under section labels, composers by birth year.
Era page: plate 124, title Literata 30, dates SF 14 ink2, one sentence in Literata 17/1.6, then Composers (a shelf of 76 pt portrait tiles, tap = ComposerSheet) and Pieces (LibraryRow; today’s piece first, then by year).
Form page: title, count, the Library’s Composer filter chip, then LibraryRows.
Back: the 44 pt glass circle used on the piece page.

s3b.text:
PREMIUM, WITHOUT NEW BADGES
Exactly the Library’s behaviour: for a free user a past piece shows the lock (18 pt, ink3) where the chevron would be and opens the paywall; today’s piece shows “· Today” and opens; a birthday gift shows “· Open today”. Rows are never dimmed. Cards and section pages carry no lock and no Premium badge: the lock appears only on the thing that is locked.
ONLY PUBLISHED PIECES
The Library holds published pieces only (20 on 28 November, one more each day), so counts and lists use the same data. All 52 composers and all six eras are listed from the start, because the biographies and era texts are ready; a piece count shows only when there is one, and an era with no piece yet shows its composers and one line. Forms appear with their first published piece (six of eleven on 28 November), with one footer line saying so.
NO NEW ENDPOINT
Everything comes from /v1/pieces and /v1/composers, which the app already loads. New: a small eras/forms data file (descriptions, collage picks), bundled and served like the glossary.
